entries.classification_evidence: ubuntu 3.14 only (4576 ran, errors=1; the same commit passed on ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13, and locally 4579 OK): the V1 test helper tests/test_closure.py::Repo.close raised OSError [Errno 39] Directory not empty: '/tmp/tmpms1248ti/.git' from TemporaryDirectory.cleanup. Measured cause (GIT_TRACE=1 on a fresh repository, git 2.53/2.55): `git commit` spawns `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`, a detached child that writes into .git while the helper is already removing the repository — a race of the V1 test harness, HARNESS: not PRODUCT (aisef/ untouched, V1 evidence byte-identical), not DEVELOPER (no V2 test, no V2 code in the traceback), not ENVIRONMENT (the runner did what git asked). No V1-PF-001 signature; owned processes 0/0/0, escaped 0, released_empty True. Not rerun: the fix candidate (the helper runs git with maintenance.auto=false and gc.auto=0) is validated by its own first run.

entries.classification_evidence: windows 3.11 only (4573 ran, errors=1; the same commit passed on ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and locally): test_memory.IntegrationTests.test_concurrent_writers, a V1 test of the frozen tree, errored with PermissionError [Errno 13] Permission denied from os.write(fd, b'\0') in aisef/_compat.py::flock_ex_nb (called by aisef/memory.py::_locked): the Windows shim writes the lock file's first byte itself when the file is empty, so two first writers racing on a brand-new store can have one write into the byte the other just locked; the shim translates only msvcrt.locking's error to BlockingIOError, never os.write's, and _locked retries BlockingIOError only. PRODUCT: a latent defect of the frozen V1 tree (aisef/ is not modified; the same test failed once before this program, D-020 notes), Windows-only, first occurrence in the V2 program's CI logs; not DEVELOPER (no V2 code, no V2 test), not HARNESS (the test's writers did what the product asks), not ENVIRONMENT. No V1-PF-001 signature; owned processes 0/0/0, escaped 0, released_empty True. Not rerun: the fix candidate seeds the lock byte in the V1 test so CI measures the twenty writers the test is about; the defect is reported for the owner's V1 backlog, not fixed.

entries.classification_evidence: windows only (4712 ran, failures=2, errors=1; ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14 PASS 4715, local 4718 OK). Two defects of the candidate's tests and evidence builder, none of the kernel: (1) the NextAndPump window case's fake range returned 'still running' (None) after a plain time.sleep; on Windows the sleep can end before the coarse monotonic clock reaches the deadline, so the reader took the None for the anchor's report closing and returned UNRUNNABLE ('Unrunnable' object has no attribute 'behavior_verdict'). The real ProcessRange.wait returns None on a timeout only once the monotonic clock has passed its deadline (queue.get), which the reader relies on; the fakes now honour that contract and a new case pins it on the real range. (2) the V2-006 evidence builder ran the POSIX-only anchor watchdog test as a race case; skipped on Windows it counted as not passing, so every_race_case_passes was false and P6-V2-006-PROBE-HARNESS.json re-derived differently (Q0: p6_evidence not calibrated). The builder now runs platform-independent cases only; the anchor watchdog stays bound structurally.
